reason: Flux-rs is the default-profile companion for refinement claims; the seed's risk_tags do not include refinement, ownership, or index. The validation is a single == 0 integer compare inside a private helper (require_non_zero_run); encoding it as a Flux refinement adds the same predicate the helper already enforces. The contract is a rejection claim (not a refinement on a type-level index/length relationship). Flux cannot add value here. See VLD-FLUX-CN2V4-001 in verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl.
boundary_proof: The Flux lane would express the same `run != 0` predicate already enforced by require_non_zero_run. Encoding this as a refinement type adds a duplicate predicate the helper enforces structurally. The contract's C2 single-guard-helper shape is the structural enforcement; Flux cannot improve the structural guarantee. The Verus mirror PO-001-VERUS-MIRROR and the proptest PO-005-PROPTEST-PER-PREFIX cover the rejection claim with stronger evidence (unbounded invariant + property pressure).
compensating_evidence: PO-005-PROPTEST-PER-PREFIX (proptest, 10000 cases per prefix across all six encoders)

reason: Loom is the default-profile companion for concurrency claims; the seed's risk_tags do not include concurrency, interleaving, cancellation, or shutdown. The encoders are pure synchronous; no Send/Sync boundary; no async; no threads. Loom's schedule exploration would find no interleavings to explore. See VLD-LOOM-CN2V4-001 in verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl.
boundary_proof: The encoders are pub fn with no shared state, no locks, no atomics, no channels, no async/await. The 19 call sites that invoke the encoders (enumerated in workflow-model.md#Error-Surface-Shift-at-Journal-Append-Call-Sites) are synchronous method calls. Loom cannot model a surface that does not exist. The Verus mirror PO-001-VERUS-MIRROR and the proptest PO-005-PROPTEST-PER-PREFIX cover the rejection claim.

reason: Miri is the default-profile companion for unsafe/UB claims; vb_storage sets #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at the crate root. No FFI, no raw pointers, no unsafe block in any encoder path. Miri cannot detect UB in a surface that does not exist. See VLD-MIRI-CN2V4-001 in verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl.
boundary_proof: The crate-level #![forbid(unsafe_code)] attribute (verified at crate root) plus rg -n 'unsafe' crates/vb_storage/src/keys.rs returning empty proves the surface is absent. Miri's UB detection operates on unsafe Rust; with no unsafe, Miri has nothing to check. The Verus mirror PO-001-VERUS-MIRROR and the Kani split-harness PO-003-KANI-SPLIT-HARNESS cover the rejection claim with stronger evidence.

reason: cargo-fuzz is the default-profile companion for parser/codec/hostile-input claims; the seed's risk_tags do not include parser, codec, or hostile_input. Encoders are typed-input (typed RunId, EventSeq, StepIdx, etc.), not byte-stream parsers. The contract explicitly notes fuzz is optional/friendly-evidence but not required (contract.md#C8 lane profile hint). proptest covers the rejection space efficiently at 10000 cases; Kani provides bounded symbolic coverage. See VLD-FUZZ-CN2V4-001 in verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl.
boundary_proof: The encoder entry points accept typed inputs (RunId, EventSeq, StepIdx, etc.) not raw bytes. The fuzz harness would need to first generate well-typed inputs (which is a proptest strategy), then call the encoder — at which point proptest covers the same surface more efficiently. The contract.md#C8 lane profile says 'No fuzz required by contract; a fuzz target is a natural friendly-evidence surface for hostile input but is optional.' The 18 test flips in contract.md#C5 (test-writer's scope) plus the proptest PO-005-PROPTEST-PER-PREFIX plus the Kani harness PO-003-KANI-SPLIT-HARNESS cover the rejection claim.
compensating_evidence: contract.md#C5 (18 test flips covering typed-input rejection in unit-test layer)
